_comment: Every tool that declares reach anyone, with the reason it is safe: the in-code guard it relies on (callers list, presence proof, own-scope check, held at the Gate), or read-only. A tool with a mutating verb in its name needs a reason that names a guard; read-only does not count. PENDING reasons are tracked and shrink. test/reach-anyone.test.js fails on an anyone with no entry.

chrome.point.reason: an agent needs the computer-use grant (requireGrant) and a posted plan (oversight guard); the URL floor refuses blind pages and password and OTP frames; an agent's call carries asked false, so an outward act holds at the Gate

computers.checkout.reason: own-scope check: resolve() limits an agent to its own computer, and the assistant is exempt as the user's own path; it only starts or thaws a computer the agent already has

computers.get.reason: own-scope check: resolve() limits an agent to its own computer; read-only

computers.giveback.reason: in-code guard: ownSurface refuses an ordinary agent, so an agent cannot end a person's take-over

computers.limits.reason: in-code guard: an agent that is not the assistant is refused inside (the user sets limits); a person and the assistant pass

computers.list.reason: own-scope check: an agent sees only its own computer; the assistant and a person see all (read-only)

computers.pause.reason: own-scope check: resolve() limits an agent to its own computer; it only pauses that computer's own hands

computers.release.reason: own-scope check: resolve() limits an agent to its own computer; it gives a screen back

computers.restart.reason: own-scope check: resolve() limits an agent to its own computer; a new container on the same home

computers.resume.reason: own-scope check: resolve() limits an agent to its own computer; it only resumes that computer's own hands

computers.stop.reason: own-scope check: resolve() limits an agent to its own computer; its home volume stays and the next checkout starts it again

computers.takeover.reason: in-code guard: ownSurface refuses an ordinary agent claiming a person's surface; the lease and the keyboard checks follow

computers.watch.reason: in-code guard: ownSurface refuses an ordinary agent (it is not a person's screen); it only hands out a one-use ticket, and refuses a computer that died

sync.delete.reason: callers list in code (cli, local, deck, capsule) and a preview unless confirm: true. Weak on its own: confirm is caller-supplied and cli or local is only as strong as the socket label, so a detached child could claim cli. The socket-trust inversion (a person label only from the owner's login session) closes that; its tests include a detached child claiming cli with confirm:true, which must be refused
